programme.title: China's concert boom: Why Gen Z is filling the stadiums
programme.desc: From packed stadium shows to sold-out performances in smaller cities, China's live music scene is expanding rapidly. Young audiences are turning concerts into a cultural routine: traveling across cities, sharing the experience online and building collective memories around live performances. The boom now extends far beyond the stage, boosting tourism, retail spending and local economies. In this episode of Unboxing China, we explore how concerts are reshaping consumption patterns and becoming a new driver of cultural and urban development.

programme.title: The self-care economy explained: How emotional spending is reshaping consumer trends
programme.desc: For months, Chinese social feeds have been filled with "Lao Ji"- a third-person way of saying "me." What began as a slang sign-off, "Love you, Lao Ji. See you tomorrow," now signals a broader shift toward self-care and emotional self-support. It also feeds a huge market where young consumers are rechanneling budgets toward small, meaningful purchases that support emotional wellbeing. In this episode of Unboxing China, we trace how a casual phrase turned into a cultural movement, reshaping consumption and mental-health talk.

programme.title: Full-chain AI fuels Yiwu's global trade boom
programme.desc: Official figures show Yiwu’s exports hit 315.4 billion yuan in the first five months, rising 9% year-on-year. The city crossed the 300-billion-yuan threshold one month earlier than last year, marking a record high for the period. Behind these impressive numbers lies Yiwu’s continuous rollout of innovative business models and new industries, which keep fueling the transformation and upgrading of its traditional trade sector.

programme.title: Inside China's push to power AI with data
programme.desc: High-quality data is emerging as the foundation of artificial intelligence (AI). In north China's Xiongan New Area, companies are building data infrastructure that supports both embodied AI – where robots learn through real-world interactions – and large AI models trained for increasingly complex tasks. CGTN's Wang Tianyu has the story.

programme.title: Xinjiang turns generation, storage, and recycling into a working model for clean power
programme.desc: China is making huge progress in clean energy and breaking records along the way. New numbers from the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region show that green energy trading more than doubled in just six months. At the same time, new projects there are testing better solar power, energy storage, and ways to recycle old wind turbine blades. It's turning the region into a real-life testing ground for the world's renewable future.

programme.title: Policy push brings smart homes into everyday life
programme.desc: China has expanded and upgraded its dual-new policy package, marking the first-ever inclusion of smart home products in central government consumption subsidies. CGTN reporter He Jingyi explores the Beijing Premium Housing Tech Expo, testing out smart home systems with voice control and automatic sensory adjustment. She also visits offline Suning stores, speaking with outlet managers and customers to uncover how smart home solutions are gaining mainstream traction, entering ordinary households, and driving the upgrade of China’s manufacturing industry.

programme.title: Behind CXMT IPO and China’s chip roadmap
programme.desc: As CXMT makes its market debut on Shanghai's STAR Market, the listing is drawing attention far beyond the trading floor. As China's top DRAM producer, CXMT sits at the center of the country's push to strengthen its semiconductor capabilities and build a more resilient technology ecosystem. What does the IPO mean for investors, the capital market, and the future of the global memory-chip industry? Join us on BizTalk as we explore market forces, policy priorities and the roadmap to technology self-reliance behind the landmark listing.

programme.title: Meet China: When Chinese Dynamism Reshapes Landscapes — Boundless Challenges, Infinite Vitality
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode shows how China’s dynamism is reshaping landscapes and lives worldwide.

programme.title: 2026 WORLD ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE CONFERENCE SPECIAL | China’s Vision for AI Development and Global Governance
programme.desc: The 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) will conclude on 20th July in Shanghai. Join CGTN Biztalk on July 20 as it invites conference participants, industry observers and researchers to discuss the outcomes of the conference, and look into how China leverages WAIC as a premier industrial platform to foster dialogue, bridge divides, and promote shared governance.

programme.title: Summer Davos 2026: The Future of Jobs, Skills, and Sustainable Growth
programme.desc: Global trade is undergoing profound change as economies grapple with shifting supply chains, rapid advances in artificial intelligence, and the transition to cleaner energy. We are coming to you from the Summer Davos Forum in Dalian, where policymakers, business leaders, and academics from around the world are discussing how to navigate these transformations. One key question at this year's forum is how these changes will affect workers, and whether they will create new opportunities or deepen existing challenges. To discuss the future of jobs, skills, and sustainable growth, Song Ruixin is joined by Professor Mercedes Maroto-Valer, Deputy Principal for Global Sustainability at Heriot-Watt University, and Kathleen Alexander, co-founder and CEO of Savor, a San Jose based food startup.

programme.title: Full-chain AI fuels Yiwu's global trade boom
programme.desc: Official figures show Yiwu’s exports hit 315.4 billion yuan in the first five months, rising 9% year-on-year. The city crossed the 300-billion-yuan threshold one month earlier than last year, marking a record high for the period. Behind these impressive numbers lies Yiwu’s continuous rollout of innovative business models and new industries, which keep fueling the transformation and upgrading of its traditional trade sector.

programme.title: Inside China's push to power AI with data
programme.desc: High-quality data is emerging as the foundation of artificial intelligence (AI). In north China's Xiongan New Area, companies are building data infrastructure that supports both embodied AI – where robots learn through real-world interactions – and large AI models trained for increasingly complex tasks. CGTN's Wang Tianyu has the story.

programme.title: Xinjiang turns generation, storage, and recycling into a working model for clean power
programme.desc: China is making huge progress in clean energy and breaking records along the way. New numbers from the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region show that green energy trading more than doubled in just six months. At the same time, new projects there are testing better solar power, energy storage, and ways to recycle old wind turbine blades. It's turning the region into a real-life testing ground for the world's renewable future.

programme.title: Policy push brings smart homes into everyday life
programme.desc: China has expanded and upgraded its dual-new policy package, marking the first-ever inclusion of smart home products in central government consumption subsidies. CGTN reporter He Jingyi explores the Beijing Premium Housing Tech Expo, testing out smart home systems with voice control and automatic sensory adjustment. She also visits offline Suning stores, speaking with outlet managers and customers to uncover how smart home solutions are gaining mainstream traction, entering ordinary households, and driving the upgrade of China’s manufacturing industry.

programme.title: Behind CXMT IPO and China’s chip roadmap
programme.desc: As CXMT makes its market debut on Shanghai's STAR Market, the listing is drawing attention far beyond the trading floor. As China's top DRAM producer, CXMT sits at the center of the country's push to strengthen its semiconductor capabilities and build a more resilient technology ecosystem. What does the IPO mean for investors, the capital market, and the future of the global memory-chip industry? Join us on BizTalk as we explore market forces, policy priorities and the roadmap to technology self-reliance behind the landmark listing.

programme.title: Suzhou Fans
programme.desc: Suzhou, known as the “Venice of China,” is also famous for its traditional crafts. And one of the most elegant and exquisite crafts is Suzhou fans. Celebrated for their exquisite design and fine quality, they’re popularly associated with literati. How come Suzhou gave birth to such a variety of fans? How can we appreciate their beauty in the modern world? In this episode, we are discovering more stories behind Suzhou fans.

programme.title: The Pulse
programme.desc: “The Pulse” features musicians performing amidst Guizhou’s stunning natural scenery, bringing to life a harmonious blend of music and landscape.

programme.title: China Bound：Xiamen
programme.desc: What's it like in one of China's happiest cities? Tianran is in sunny Xiamen on China's southeast coast, visiting the city's famous "island of music" and sampling local delicacies like shark meatballs, shacha noodles and fish in "soy sauce water". He'll discover former fishing villages turned hipster havens, drink tea with locals beneath traditional tenement buildings, and visit a student enclave brimming with creative startup energy.

programme.title: Shunde’s Waterways: where business smarts meet everyday life-0
programme.desc: Shunde, a district in Guangdong Province, lies in the Pearl River Delta, north of Hong Kong—a water-rich region that lives by water and knows how to turn it into opportunity. Once, boats carried silk down its canals from small villages, building a legacy of trade. Today, Xiangyunsha (gambiered Canton gauze) is a global fashion icon, and historic spots like Mingshi Garden draw tourists and locals alike. With water as their muse and grit as their guide, Shunde folks keep business thriving while making life sweeter—that’s the quiet wisdom flowing through their rivers. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia are setting out to explore more with the locals...

programme.title: Foodwise: Shantou
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in Shantou, Guangdong Province in south China, where they drink more tea than anywhere else in the country. They'll savor the complex aroma of the curiously named "Duck Poo Fragrance" tea, as well as enjoy a more traditional "yum cha" breakfast. They get a taste of traditional handicrafts, from breaking bowls to make inlaid porcelain to rolling "kueh" rice cakes, and feast on everything from sweet and savory street snacks to the finest seafood dining.

programme.title: Foodwise: Shaoguan
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in the picturesque city of Shaoguan in Guangdong Province, South China. They try tea grown on Danxia landforms and feast on mountain produce, before getting hands-on with making rice noodles in a Hakka walled village. They learn about the Hakka people’s southward migration and the effect it had on local tea and food, and end their journey in a thousand-year-old Buddhist temple, seeing how the monks integrate their practice into everyday life, and discovering just why tea is so important to Zen.

programme.title: Aerial China: Beijing
programme.desc: China’s capital of Beijing is a bucket list city for any self-styled world traveler, but let’s be honest, not all of us have the time! Not to worry, because we’re about to embark on an aerial journey over the nation’s heart, giving you a crash course on this massive hub of culture, international exchange, and technological innovation. If you’re afraid of heights, this may be the one time it’s okay to look down!

programme.title: Life in the Cloud
programme.desc: The second episode faithfully records what Tianran sees and feels during the backpacking tour in Danba County, Garze Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan Province. The perseverance, sincerity and hospitality of the people in Xizang leave a profound impression on the travelers visiting this land.

programme.title: Shunde’s Waterways: where business smarts meet everyday life-0
programme.desc: Shunde, a district in Guangdong Province, lies in the Pearl River Delta, north of Hong Kong—a water-rich region that lives by water and knows how to turn it into opportunity. Once, boats carried silk down its canals from small villages, building a legacy of trade. Today, Xiangyunsha (gambiered Canton gauze) is a global fashion icon, and historic spots like Mingshi Garden draw tourists and locals alike. With water as their muse and grit as their guide, Shunde folks keep business thriving while making life sweeter—that’s the quiet wisdom flowing through their rivers. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia are setting out to explore more with the locals...

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-1 Baji Quan
programme.desc: In the first episode of Season 2 of Kung Fu Wise, Baji Quan, host Kleber travels to Mengcun, Cangzhou, in Hebei Province. There, he meets Wu Hao, the young head of the Wu-style Baji Quan school. Together, they journey across the North China Plain, from bustling village markets and the family training hall to the Bohai Sea coast, as Kleber experiences Baji Quan’s explosive power first-hand. Along the way, the episode unpacks the idea of “opening the gate”, the key to focused power, and the spirit of spear work. It goes beyond technique to reveal Cangzhou’s rich martial heritage, tracing how Wu-style Baji Quan has travelled from its hometown to Europe, proof that traditional kung fu can endure, evolve, and thrive today. In the end, Wu Hao answers with action: true inheritance is not only about skills, but about shaping spirit and character.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But ?there’s more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise. Kleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan’s narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals

programme.title: Chengdu Lacquerware Art
programme.desc: Chengdu lacquerware is unique, thanks to its “three carvings and one engraving” technique. Along with its bold decorative style, this has made it a gem of Chinese lacquer art. Chengdu lacquerware also emphasizes the use of vibrant colors. Pieces are brought to beautiful life by bright red, vivid yellow, emerald green, and other striking hues.

programme.title: The Pulse
programme.desc: “The Pulse” features musicians performing amidst Guizhou’s stunning natural scenery, bringing to life a harmonious blend of music and landscape.

programme.title: China Bound：Xiamen
programme.desc: What's it like in one of China's happiest cities? Tianran is in sunny Xiamen on China's southeast coast, visiting the city's famous "island of music" and sampling local delicacies like shark meatballs, shacha noodles and fish in "soy sauce water". He'll discover former fishing villages turned hipster havens, drink tea with locals beneath traditional tenement buildings, and visit a student enclave brimming with creative startup energy.

programme.title: Shunde's flavors: where tradition blends with vivid daily life-0
programme.desc: Shunde, a gastronomic gem in the Pearl River Delta, neighboring Hong Kong, uses masterful craft and sincere heart to transform local treasures – from crispy fish skin to fried milk – into culinary wonders. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia, are setting out to taste the flavors and feel the warmth of Shunde's countryside with the locals.

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing
programme.desc: From the local delicacies of Beijing's Ox Street to latest hangouts and contemporary cuisine of the Chinese capital, hosts Tianran He and Eva May will give you a true taste of Beijing, and the fascinating stories and people behind them.

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing's Hutongs
programme.desc: The Hutongs in Beijing are considered the city's blood vessels, as these traditional alleyways make up the DNA of the capital for its rich history and culture. In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May zigzag their way through the Hutongs and the Forbidden City for a mouth-watering experience full of ancient and modern delicacies. Starring German designer Katrin, Russian artist Liuba and photographer Feng Yu from Beijing, our hosts are taking you along a journey that features fried noodles, dim sum, pancakes and co.!

programme.title: Bird's-eye China : Shanghai
programme.desc: Balancing delicately on an alluvial plain and the Yangtze estuary of China’s east coast, much of Shanghai-literally meaning “on the sea”-sits at an average sea-level elevation of about 4 meters. Bisecting the city is the Huangpu River, dividing it into Puxi (west bank) and Pudong (east bank), where you’ll find its famous international airport. Join us as on an aerial cruise as we journey upstream towards one of the world’s most recognizable skylines.

programme.title: A Magic Chinese New Year
programme.desc: During the Year‑of‑the‑Ox Spring Festival, we visited Gubei Water Town in Miyun District, Beijing. Join host He Tianran to experience an authentic northern‑style Spring Festival. We will paste paper lanterns, cut paper‑cut window decorations, watch sugar‑blowing craftsmanship and release sky lanterns. Let us embrace this blessed Year of the Ox together.

programme.title: Shunde's flavors: where tradition blends with vivid daily life-0
programme.desc: Shunde, a gastronomic gem in the Pearl River Delta, neighboring Hong Kong, uses masterful craft and sincere heart to transform local treasures – from crispy fish skin to fried milk – into culinary wonders. programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-2 Chinese Wrestling
programme.desc: In Episode 2, Chinese Wrestling, host Kleber joins a public training session led by Wang Tongqing, a master preserving the imperial Shanpu Ying wrestling tradition. Swept up in the group’s lively atmosphere, he gets a first-hand feel for the master’s skill. Kleber then invites his Italian friend Paolo to train systematically, uncovering how Chinese wrestling principles connect with other martial arts, from Tai Chi to Wing Chun. Through Master Wang’s story of bringing a formerly imperial martial art into the public sphere, mentoring the next generation, and hoping to take it onto the international stage, the episode shows wrestling as more than a test of strength. It is a cultural bridge between history and the present.

programme.desc: Dan discovers a series of anomalies in Tutankhamun's burial, and spots that the faces on his coffins and canopic jars do not match that of the famous golden mask. Raksha looks at Seti's tomb, which shows how hurried Tutankhamun's was in comparison.

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Egypt
programme.desc: From the statues of Rameses II to the final flourishes under Queen Cleopatra, Sooke discovers that the subsequent invasions by foreign rulers, from the Nubians and Alexander the Great to the Romans, produced a new hybrid art full of surprise.

programme.title: Walking with Beasts
programme.desc: Special effects-filled documentary beginning 49 million years ago. The world is heavily forested and birds rule the planet, preying on small mammals. Whales have not yet evolved, and their ancestors walk on the land.

programme.title: Walking with Beasts
programme.desc: A pregnant basilosaurus, an 18-metre, carnivorous whale which lives in the Tethys Sea, is forced to kill the young of a smaller whale to ensure the survival of her unborn calf.

programme.title: Walking with Beasts
programme.desc: Going back 25 million years to the time of the indricothere, which was the largest mammal ever to live on dry land, being seven metres high and weighing 15 tons! The only threat to an adult would have been the Hyaenodon which was the size of a rhino.

programme.title: Walking with Beasts
programme.desc: The beginnings of mankind can be traced back 3.2 million years to Ethiopia and the advent of Australopithecus, a type of ape which, like humans, was bipedal. These early members of the human family faced many dangers, including the sabre-toothed cat.

programme.title: Science of Walking With Beasts
programme.desc: This episode explains how the 120-million-year reign of the dinosaurs ended when mammals became the fastest and fiercest creatures on the planet.

programme.title: Science of Walking With Beasts
programme.desc: A look at the science that has proved Darwin's idea that intelligent, sophisticated humans have an ancestral connection with the ape.

programme.title: Walking With Cavemen
programme.desc: The lives of cavemen were nasty, brutish and short, but somehow they evolved over 3.5 million years into Homo sapiens.

programme.title: Bright Now S1
programme.desc: Alleen al in de Verenigde Staten worden elke dag meer dan 400 miljoen kopjes koffie gedronken (warm of koud), waardoor het een van de populairste dranken is. Experts onthullen enkele van de verrassende geheimen die ervoor zorgen dat je favoriete koffie smaakt zoals hij smaakt.

programme.title: Bright Now S1
programme.desc: De medewerkers van het Zuid-Afrikaanse Manyoni Private Game Reserve zorgen met passie voor enkele van de meest bijzondere en bedreigde wilde dieren ter wereld. Van het behandelen van voetinfecties bij olifanten tot het testen van cheeta's op tuberculose, ze weten nooit wat ze kunnen verwachten.

programme.title: Backyard Ballistics S1
programme.desc: Jörg & Cheyenne worden uitgedaagd om een bijlvliegmachine te bouwen. Cheyenne werkt aan de bijl en Jörg aan de nodige berekeningen. Dit is geen eenvoudige klus! Kunnen ze er een van de beste bijlengooiers van het VK mee verslaan in de wedstrijd?

programme.title: The Re-Inventors S1
programme.desc: Het ziet eruit als een hondenhok op grote natte wetsuit, maar deze uitvinding uit 1916 had talloze levens op zee kunnen redden.

programme.title: The Re-Inventors S1
programme.desc: Een persoonlijke brandtrap voor mensen die vastzitten in gebouwen: het moet werken als je het nodig hebt. Zal het je leven redden of niet? Laten we eens kijken.

programme.title: The Re-Inventors S1
programme.desc: Een stalen helm met een luchtdrukgeweer erop gemonteerd. Wat kan er misgaan?

programme.title: The Lightbulb Moment S1
programme.desc: Toen iemand bij Mark Zuckerberg van Facebook voor het eerst de Like-knop opperde, had hij een simpel antwoord: "Nee."

programme.title: The Lightbulb Moment S1
programme.desc: Futuristisch ontwerper Robert Propst, droomde van de 'Action Office' als een werkplekutopie die het onbenutte potentieel van de hedendaagse kenniswerker zou verwezenlijken.

programme.title: The Lightbulb Moment S1
programme.desc: Barcodes hebben de wereldhandel radicaal veranderd en de opkomst van gigantische bedrijven als Walmart en wereldmachten als China bevorderd.

programme.title: Women Make Science S1
programme.desc: Anastasia Miliou en haar team van vrouwelijke wetenschappers bouwen in Griekenland het allereerste opvangcentrum voor dolfijnen die uit gevangenschap zijn vrijgelaten.

programme.title: Women Make Science S1
programme.desc: Een van 's werelds grootste tech-ontwikkelaars creëert een nieuwe generatie robots die ontworpen zijn om mensen te helpen met alledaagse taken.

programme.title: Silly Sustainability S1
programme.sub-title: Can You Power A Lawnmower With Grass?
programme.desc: Andy van het YouTubekanaal 'How To Make Everything' test of hij maaisel van het maaien van zijn gazon kan gebruiken om brandstof te maken die de grasmaaier aandrijft die hij daarvoor gebruikt.

programme.title: Silly Sustainability S1
programme.desc: In onze nieuwe serie met Andy van 'How To Make Everything', onderzoeken we of huishoudelijke recyclebare materialen kunnen worden omgezet in houtvervangers.

programme.title: Silly Sustainability S1
programme.desc: In onze nieuwe serie met Andy van 'How To Make Everything', onderzoeken we hoe je bouwmaterialen in massa kunt vervaardigen uit recyclebare huishoudmaterialen.

programme.title: The New Frontier S3
programme.desc: De LISA pathfinder heeft het mogelijk gemaakt om zwaartekrachtgolfdetectors in de ruimte te krijgen. Wat zijn zwaartekrachtgolven precies en waarom zijn ze zo moeilijk te detecteren?

programme.title: Xploration Outer Space S7
programme.sub-title: Unsolved Mysteries of the Solar System
programme.desc: Hoewel er ruimteschepen naar elke planeet in ons zonnestelsel zijn gestuurd, blijven er nog veel mysteries over. Presentatrice Emily Calandrelli gaat op zoek naar antwoorden op hemelse mysteries die zelfs onze slimste wetenschappers niet kunnen beantwoorden.

programme.title: Breakthrough S1
programme.desc: Het verhaal van de wetenschap achter de grootste, geavanceerdste en duurste telescoop ooit gemaakt.

programme.title: Breakthrough S1
programme.sub-title: First Images: The James Webb Telescope
programme.desc: Een nieuw tijdperk in de sterrenkunde is aangebroken nu de wereld voor het eerst de volledige capaciteiten van NASA's James Webb-ruimtetelescoop kan zien. De eerste beelden van 's werelds grootste en krachtigste ruimtetelescoop tonen Webb in zijn volle potentie.

programme.title: Breakthrough S1
programme.desc: Dit is een kijkje in NASA's baanbrekende Artemis-programma, het ruimteschip en de mensen die de mensheid een stap dichter bij de maan, Mars en verder zullen brengen.

programme.title: Secrets of the Factories S1
programme.desc: De McVitie’s-fabriek in Carlisle, Cumbria, opent haar deuren en laat zien hoe miljoenen van ’s lands favoriete koekjes worden gemaakt — 24 uur per dag — in een van de grootste fabrieken van Groot-Brittannië én de oudste koekjesfabriek ter wereld.

programme.title: Secrets of the Factories S1
programme.desc: Van het maken van verse spaghetti en het mengen van de geheime ingrediënten voor de saus tot gigantische geautomatiseerde kranen en de nieuwste robots: ga vandaag nog aan de slag bij de Heinz-fabriek en maak samen met de machines van morgen blikken met favoriete producten voor thuis.

programme.title: Secrets of the Factories S1
programme.desc: Ontdek wat er allemaal bij komt kijken om tot wel 5 miljoen cakes per dag te maken, waaronder French Fancies, Angel Slices en Bramley Apple Pies. Maak kennis met de ingenieurs die de machines 24/7 draaiende houden, de medewerkers die de cakes produceren en de operators die dagelijks met ultramoderne robots werken.

programme.title: Heavy Lifting S1
programme.desc: Dave krijgt te maken met een rommelige trein, J.P. zaagt een boom om, Regional Crane tilt een enorme muur en Maxum Crane verplaatst een bank naar een hoog gebouw.

programme.title: Heavy Lifting S1
programme.desc: Dave staat voor een lastige lift bij een woning, J.P. racet tussen last-minute klussen door, en Brad en Nathan Moore helpen een familie hun droom waar te maken.
